comparisons.peer_topic: High Quality Liquid Assets and Liquidity Coverage Ratio
comparisons.peer_summary: Global Liquidity Sources are substantially the same in composition as High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) under U.S. Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) rules, though HQLA is calculated at a lower value incorporating regulatory deductions. The company's average consolidated HQLA was $623 billion and $590 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, resulting in average consolidated LCRs of 113 percent and 115 percent respectively, with fluctuations attributed to normal business flows.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that their average High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) increased in the fourth quarter of 2024. However, Citi attributes this increase primarily to an increase in average wholesale funding, whereas Bank of America reports specific dollar amounts for average consolidated HQLA ($623 billion) and an average consolidated LCR of 113 percent for the same period, noting that its Global Liquidity Sources are substantially the same in composition as HQLA.

sentences.text: Citigroup's average HQLA increased quarter-over-quarter as of the fourth quarter of 2024, primarily driven by an increase in average wholesale funding.
Our average consolidated HQLA, on a net basis, was $623 billion and $590 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023.
For the same periods, the average consolidated LCR was 113 percent and 115 percent.

comparisons.peer_topic: Exclusion of Bank Excess HQLA from Firm Reporting
comparisons.peer_summary: Under the LCR rule, excess eligible HQLA held by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. that cannot be transferred to non-bank affiliates is excluded from the Firm's reported eligible HQLA.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase discuss the regulatory treatment of HQLA held at specific subsidiaries. Citi notes that its HQLA table includes amounts needed to meet minimum requirements at operating entities as well as excess amounts available for transfer within the group. JPMorgan Chase specifically details that under the LCR rule, excess eligible HQLA held by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. that is not transferable to non-bank affiliates must be excluded from the Firm's reported eligible HQLA.
